title: Sixteen Winters and One Short Stone
subtitle: 古代文明 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 古代文明（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）
meta: 主题语境：古代文明（人与社会·历史、社会与文化）　|　核心词汇：era　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 era 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1887 my great-uncle ① opened an era that no scholar in the city would have dated, and he said the opening was the whole of the winter. The ② era, meaning the age itself and not the year, ran sixteen winters and stayed undated in the book; an era, he said, is the only thing in a city that is judged by how long it is left undated.

Every ③ era in that city had the same short stone beside it, and the ④ era at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the temple and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An era, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to date; my great-uncle said the dating is the part that fills sixteen winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the era was the whole of the dig, meaning the period and not the age. The ⑥ era, meaning the period and not any of that, is the only thing in a dig that everybody waits for and nobody dates; era, he said, is either something you open or the only word that means both an age and a period. He said the period is the part they remember.

By 1895 the ⑦ era had become a line in a table, and the table had become an argument about the short stone. The ⑧ era of the whole thing, my great-uncle wrote in January, was one city and sixteen winters of dating; era, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to date. He said the dating was never mentioned.

The ⑨ era I remember is the one dated in the table, which closed in 1903 and is still described as the quietest in the city. An ⑩ era, my mother said in 1905, is the only one that improves by being dated; every era, she said, is a period that has agreed to look like an age. She said the period was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 时代；年代（指城里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 时代（指那一个本身，与年份相对）
C. 固定搭配：open an era 开启一个时代
D. n. 时代（指留给神庙的那一个）
E. n. 时代（抽象总称，指一座城里的纪年之事）
F. n. 时代（指年表上写到、被断代的那一个）
G. n. 历史时期（指发掘中人人都在等却无人断代的那样东西）
H. n. 时期（抽象总称，指人人都在等却无人断代的那样东西）

items.q: opened an era that no scholar in the city would have dated
The era, meaning the age itself and not the year
the era at the far side
the era was the whole of the dig
the era had become a line in a table
The era of the whole thing
An era, my mother said in 1905

answers.why: open an era 意为“开启一个时代”，1887 年曾叔父开启了一个城里没有一位学者肯断代的时代。
era 意为“时代”，指那一个本身而不是年份，它经过了十六个冬天而在簿子上没有日期。
era 意为“时代”，指城里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一块短短的石碑。
era 意为“时代”，指留给神庙的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
era 意为“历史时期”，指发掘中人人都在等却无人断代的那样东西，叔叔说这个时期就是那次发掘的全部。
era 意为“时期”，指人人都在等却无人断代的那样东西而不是那一个时代，是发掘里人人都等、却无人断代的东西。
era 意为“时代”，指年表上写到、被断代的那一个，到 1895 年这一个成了年表里的一行。
era 意为“时代”，曾叔父一月写道，整件事的纪年之事是一座城和十六个冬天的断代。
era 意为“时代”，我记得的是年表上断代的那一个，1903 年结束了，至今仍被说成城里最安静的一个。
era 为抽象总称，母亲 1905 年说，一个时代是唯一会因为被好好断代而变得更好的东西。
